answer: Collateral exclusivity keeps one deposit from backing many seats. Every identity enters through a single bonding inlet that locks 50 POA and publishes a nullifier derived from those exact coins; a second identity presenting a bond whose nullifier is already listed is refused. A farm of 100 fakes therefore needs 100 separately locked bonds, 5,000 POA idle at once, and a lender cannot rent one bond to several seats. Nor can it forge a fresh nullifier without moving new coins in. Recycled collateral is the hidden reef this registry exposes, so each extra fake pays the full bond again.
